WITH patient_pics AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(PIC) as avg_pic
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
),
patient_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(CAST(HGB AS FLOAT) / CAST(HCT AS FLOAT)) as avg_ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
global_avg_ratio AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as global_avg
  FROM patient_ratios
)
SELECT
  AVG(pp.avg_pic) as avg_of_avg_pic,
  AVG(pr.avg_ratio) as avg_of_avg_ratio,
  AVG(pr.avg_ratio - gar.global_avg) as avg_excess_ratio
FROM patient_pics pp
JOIN patient_ratios pr ON pp.ID = pr.ID
CROSS JOIN global_avg_ratio gar
WHERE pr.avg_ratio > gar.global_avg

assumptions.assumption: Average PIC is computed across *all* Laboratory records for each patient (including records where HGB or HCT is missing). The 'ignoring missing values' phrase applies specifically to the ratio calculation.
Patients without any records containing both HGB and HCT values are excluded from the final result, since they cannot have a valid ratio for comparison to the global average.
Patients whose ratio exactly equals the global average are excluded ('above the average' means strict inequality).

alternatives.interpretation: Both average PIC and average ratio are computed using only Laboratory records where both HGB and HCT are not NULL (restrict to the same record subset for both metrics).
alternatives.sql:
WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(PIC) as avg_pic,
    AVG(CAST(HGB AS FLOAT) / CAST(HCT AS FLOAT)) as avg_ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
global_avg_ratio AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as global_avg
  FROM patient_stats
)
SELECT
  AVG(ps.avg_pic) as avg_of_avg_pic,
  AVG(ps.avg_ratio) as avg_of_avg_ratio,
  AVG(ps.avg_ratio - gar.global_avg) as avg_excess_ratio
FROM patient_stats ps
CROSS JOIN global_avg_ratio gar
WHERE ps.avg_ratio > gar.global_avg
